newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares firm on low liquidity, U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares firm on low liquidity, U.S. data.

text.p: Russian shares closed up on pre-holiday buying and positive U.S. economic data on Tuesday, traders said, predicting the market would continue to move upwards, despite light volumes, ahead of the long weekend.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index closed at 305.53 on a light total market turnover of $22.4 million. The index closed on Monday at 301.54.
National power company UES EESR.RTS rose to $0.2380 from $0.2305 at the close on Monday. Regional utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS rose to $1.292 from $1.265.
Oil company Surgutneftegaz SNGS.RTS edged up to $0.730 from $0.701 while international long-distance telecom Rostelekom RTKM.RTS rose to $3.6 from $3.53.

UES announced on Tuesday consolidated 1996 pre-tax profits of 11 trillion roubles calculated according to Russian accounting standards on an accruals basis and a five-rouble dividend on ordinary and preferred shares, unchanged from 1995.

But Brunswick trader Gary Kinsey said the release of the U.S. Employment Cost Index, a key indicator of wage inflation, showing a lower than expected first quarter 0.6 percent rise, also boosted prices. This reduces expectations of another U.S. interest rate rise in the near future.

"UES has been very busy all day, but a little bit later the US numbers came through and we saw more buyers of broader stocks in ADR form," Kinsey said, adding that the UES figures were in line with expectations.
Dealers said a number of second-tier shares, especially small regional telecoms, were doing well on encouraging 1996 financial results released recently.

But traders said Russian and domestic investors were building up positions in the liquidity-driven market ahead of holidays May 1-4 and 9-11 when shares will be harder to find. Many expect a general market pickup towards the end of May.
"Everyone is buying before the holidays hoping the market will rise further," said CentreInvest Securities trader Sergei Bukin. "It is speculative."
